mainTopic: The prohibition of הקפה: doubtful shavings, שמואל's 'a woman or a קטן,' and the argument between רב הונא and רב אדא about shaving a child's head.
overview: The גמרא finishes a proof from the משנה's words 'I do not know which one of you.' It then asks how both נזירים in that doubtful case may shave, since the pure one would be breaking the prohibition of הקפה. שמואל answers that the משנה is talking about a woman or a קטן. Because he did not simply say that shaving the whole head is not הקפה, the גמרא concludes that he holds it is. מר זוטרא places the same answer of שמואל on a later משנה, about a doubtful נזיר and doubtful מצורע who shaves four times. Next, רב הונא rules that an adult who rounds a קטן's head is liable, and רב אדא בר אהבה argues with him. The story ends with a curse on רב הונא's children. The גמרא explains the dispute: רב הונא ties הקפה to destroying the beard, so women are exempt, while רב אדא ties the one who shaves to the one being shaved, so shaving a קטן is not punishable. Finally, the גמרא begins asking whether the whole-head question is an argument among תנאים, quoting a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from the words 'I do not know which one of you'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier proof by pointing to the משנה's wording, 'I do not know which one of you,' and accepts the point.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is shown by the משנה saying 'But I do not know which one of you.' Conclude from it that this is correct.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up a proof that began earlier. It points to the exact words of the משנה and says 'שמע מינה,' meaning the point is proven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witness in the משנה says 'I do not know which one of you' became impure. That wording shows he did not see clearly which נזיר it was, which supports the reading the גמרא was building. 'שמע מינה' closes the discussion and accepts that reading.

keyTerms.meaning: But I do not know which one of you
Conclude from it; the point is proven

phrases.english: As it teaches: 'But I do not know which one of you.'
phrases.notes: These are the words of the witness in the משנה, telling the two נזירים that one of them became impure.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a proof that began before this section, on the previous discussion of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The reading of the משנה that the witness did not clearly see which נזיר became impure.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of the משנה: 'ואיני יודע איזה מכם.'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The inference from the משנה's wording is accepted (שמע מינה).

steps.title: Why may both shave if one may be pure?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says both נזירים shave and bring offerings. The גמרא asks: one of them may be pure, so his shaving would break the prohibition of הקפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said they shave and bring offerings. But why? Perhaps they are not both impure, and then the pure one is doing הקפה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that both נזירים shave. It challenges this, since one of them might not need to shave at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one of the two became impure, and nobody knows which. So one of them is shaving with no real need. Shaving the head that way counts as הקפה (rounding the sides of the head), which the Torah forbids. So how can the משנה tell both of them to shave?

keyTerms.meaning: Rounding the head, meaning shaving the sides (the corners) of the head, which the Torah forbids

steps.confusionAlert: Normally a נזיר is allowed to shave his whole head at the end of his נזירות or after becoming impure, because the Torah commands it. The problem here is only for the נזיר who is actually pure. For him, the shaving is not a command, so the regular prohibition applies.

phrases.english: They shave and bring offerings.
But why?
Perhaps they are not both impure,
and then he is doing rounding of the head!
phrases.notes: 'He' means whichever of the two is really pure. See ויקרא 19:27.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question on the next ruling of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that both נזירים in the doubtful case shave.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One of the two is really pure. His shaving is not a מצוה for him, so it breaks the prohibition of הקפה.

steps.title: שמואל: the case is a woman or a minor
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the משנה is talking about נזירים who are women or minors, for whom הקפה is not forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: the משנה is talking about a woman or a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the challenge by narrowing the case in the משנה. The two נזירים are women or minors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman is not included in the prohibition of הקפה. A קטן is not yet obligated in מצוות. So even if one of them shaves for no reason, no prohibition is broken, and the משנה's ruling works.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman, who is not included in the prohibition of הקפה
A minor, who is not yet obligated in מצוות

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
It is about a woman or a minor.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to people who are not bound by the prohibition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be about ordinary adult male נזירים, who are forbidden to do הקפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about a woman or a קטן, so the possibly needless shaving breaks no prohibition.

steps.title: Why not say it is an adult and the whole head is not rounding?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל didn't keep the משנה about an adult man and explain that shaving the entire head is not considered הקפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him explain the משנה as talking about an adult man, and say that shaving the whole head is not called הקפה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes on שמואל's answer. It suggests a simpler answer that would not limit the משנה to women and minors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could argue that the Torah only forbids shaving the sides of the head while leaving the rest. Shaving the whole head would then not be הקפה at all. If so, even an adult man could shave, so why did שמואל need to limit the case?

keyTerms.meaning: And let him establish it (explain the case) as
An adult, a male who has reached majority

phrases.english: But let him explain it as an adult male,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַקָּפַת כׇּל הָרֹאשׁ — לֹא שְׁמָהּ הַקָּפָה!
phrases.english: and rounding the entire head is not called rounding!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges why שמואל chose his narrower answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's choice to limit the משנה to a woman or a קטן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There seems to be a simpler answer that keeps the משנה about adult men: shaving the whole head may not be הקפה at all.

steps.title: שמואל holds that shaving the whole head is rounding
steps.stepSummary: Since שמואל did not give that simpler answer, the גמרא concludes he holds that shaving the entire head does count as הקפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the fact that he did not explain it that way, conclude that שמואל holds that shaving the whole head is called הקפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question of step 4 into a conclusion about שמואל's view. His silence tells us what he holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמואל thought shaving the whole head was allowed, he would have used that easier answer. He chose to limit the case to women and minors instead. So he must hold that shaving the entire head is forbidden as הקפה.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that he does not explain it this way
It is called rounding (it counts as הקפה)

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, shaving the entire head counts as הקפה. That is why a doubtful shaving is only allowed for a woman or a קטן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets שמואל's position on a real question about the prohibition of הקפה: does shaving the whole head count, or only shaving the sides? The answer comes out of how he chose to answer a question on a משנה.

phrases.english: From the fact that he does not explain it this way,
conclude from it that Shmuel holds:
rounding the entire head is called rounding.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּלָא מוֹקֵים לַהּ הָכִי, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ קָסָבַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 4 by drawing a conclusion about שמואל's opinion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל holds that הקפת כל הראש counts as הקפה.

steps.title: מר זוטרא places שמואל's answer on a different משנה
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא teaches שמואל's answer about a different משנה. That משנה is about a נזיר who is a doubtful טמא and a doubtful מצורע מוחלט, who eats קדשים after sixty days and shaves four times.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא taught this teaching of שמואל on a later ruling: a נזיר who may be impure, and who may be a confirmed מצורע, may eat sacrificial food after sixty days and shaves four times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of where שמואל's teaching belongs. This step sets up the case, and the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, שמואל was not answering a question on the משנה of the two נזירים. He was answering a question on a later משנה. There, a person who is in doubt about being a טמא נזיר and in doubt about being a מצורע shaves four times. One shaving is for the doubtful impurity, one is at the end of his נזירות, and two are for being a מצורע. Many of these shavings may be unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause or later ruling
A confirmed מצורע (declared definitely impure by the כהן)

phrases.english: Mar Zutra teaches it,
this teaching of Shmuel, on the latter clause:
A nazirite who was impure in doubt
and a confirmed leper in doubt
eats sacrificial food after sixty days,
and shaves four shavings.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא מַתְנֵי לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא דִּשְׁמוּאֵל אַסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of where שמואל's answer (step 3) was said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר who is a doubtful טמא and a doubtful מצורע מוחלט eats קדשים after sixty days and shaves four times.

steps.title: But he is rounding his head
steps.stepSummary: The same problem is raised on the later משנה: some of those four shavings may be unneeded, so they would break the prohibition of הקפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the later משנה. It is the same kind of challenge as in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every shaving in this case rests on a doubt. If the person is not really a טמא נזיר, or not really a מצורע, then some of his shavings are not מצוות. Those shavings would be forbidden הקפה.

phrases.english: But he is doing rounding of the head!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The later משנה's ruling that the doubtful נזיר and מצורע shaves four times.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some of the four shavings may not be required. An unneeded shaving breaks the prohibition of הקפה.

steps.title: שמואל again: a woman or a minor
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the later משנה is also talking about a woman or a קטן, who are not bound by the prohibition of הקפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: the משנה is talking about a woman or a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The same answer of שמואל is given, but now on the later משנה. This is מר זוטרא's version of where שמואל said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the four shavings are allowed because the person is a woman or a קטן. So even an unneeded shaving breaks no prohibition. The answer is the same as in step 3; only the משנה it answers is different.

keyTerms.meaning: About a woman or a minor, people not bound by the prohibition of הקפה

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of where שמואל's answer 'באשה וקטן' was said: on the משנה of the two נזירים, or (according to מר זוטרא) on the later משנה of the doubtful נזיר and מצורע. In both, the point is that an unneeded shaving is only allowed for a woman or a קטן.
steps.confusionAlert: The Aramaic of this answer is word-for-word the same as step 3. It is not a repeat of the same discussion. It is מר זוטרא's version, which places שמואל's answer on a different משנה.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
It is about a woman or a minor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 within מר זוטרא's version.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to people who are not bound by the prohibition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The later משנה seemed to be about an adult man, for whom unneeded shavings would be forbidden הקפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The later משנה is talking about a woman or a קטן, so the doubtful shavings break no prohibition.

steps.title: An adult who rounds a child's head is liable
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a person who rounds the head of a קטן is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: One who rounds the head of a minor is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a new ruling: if an adult rounds a קטן's head, the adult is punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קטן himself is not bound by הקפה, but רב הונא says the adult doing the shaving still breaks the איסור. So the child's exemption does not protect the person who does the shaving.

keyTerms.meaning: the one who rounds (shaves the corners of) someone's head
a minor, a child under בר מצוה

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
One who rounds the head of a minor
is liable.
phrases.notes: He means the adult doing the shaving, even though the child himself is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הַמַּקִּיף אֶת הַקָּטָן הֲרֵי הוּא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on שמואל's point that a קטן is not bound by הקפה, and adds a ruling about the adult who shaves him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An adult who rounds a קטן's head is liable for הקפה.

steps.title: Who shaves your own sons?
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה challenges רב הונא: if adults may not round a child's head, who shaves your children?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said to רב הונא: And your sons, who shaves them?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה pushes back on רב הונא by asking about his own family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Children's heads were normally shaved. If רב הונא forbids any adult from doing it, it seems impossible to do in his own home. The question is really an attack on his ruling.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said to Rav Huna:
And your own sons, who shaves them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that an adult who rounds a קטן is liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every adult is forbidden, nobody could shave רב הונא's own children, so the ruling seems unworkable.

steps.title: My wife חובה shaves them
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that his wife חובה does it, since a woman is not bound by הקפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: חובה (my wife shaves them).
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers with one word: his wife חובה shaves the boys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא holds that women are not included in the איסור of הקפה at all. So a woman may shave a boy's head with no problem, and his ruling still works in practice.

phrases.english: He said to him: Chova.
phrases.notes: חובה was רב הונא's wife, and as a woman she isn't bound by הקפה.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical answer: someone who is not bound by the איסור does the shaving.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed no one could shave רב הונא's children.
steps.terutzMaskana: A woman, who is not bound by הקפה, may do it.

steps.title: The curse and what followed
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא angrily curses חובה, and the גמרא reports that רב הונא's children did not survive during רב אדא's lifetime.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let חובה bury her sons. All the years of רב אדא בר אהבה, רב הונא's children did not survive.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא reacts strongly against רב הונא's answer, and the גמרא tells us the sad result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא reacts sharply to רב הונא's answer and curses חובה. The גמרא does not say exactly what upset him, but the story shows how strongly he rejected רב הונא's position. The גמרא explains the reasoning behind each side's view right afterward (steps 13–15).

phrases.english: Let Chova bury her sons.

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלְּהוּ שְׁנֵי דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
phrases.english: All the years of Rav Adda bar Ahava

phrases.aramaic: לָא אִקַּיַּים לֵיהּ זַרְעָא לְרַב הוּנָא.
phrases.english: Rav Huna's children did not survive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב אדא's reaction to רב הונא's answer, plus the outcome of the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אדא strongly rejected רב הונא's practice, and the curse took effect during his lifetime.

steps.title: What exactly do they argue about?
steps.stepSummary: Both agree that shaving the whole head counts as הקפה, so the גמרא asks what their real argument is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, since both hold that rounding the entire head is called rounding, about what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next steps by asking for the real reason behind each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides treat shaving a child's head as a real הקפה question. That means both hold that shaving the whole head counts as הקפה, like the conclusion about שמואל in step 5. So their argument must be about something else: who is included in the איסור.

phrases.english: Now, since both of them hold
that rounding the entire head is called rounding,
about what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ סְבִירָא הַקָּפַת כׇּל הָרֹאשׁ שְׁמָהּ הַקָּפָה, בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the story to ask for the reasoning of each side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying reason each אמורא gives for his ruling.

steps.title: רב הונא: rounding is tied to destroying the beard
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא learns from the פסוק that only someone included in השחתת זקן is included in הקפה, so women are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא holds: "You shall not round the corners of your head and you shall not destroy the corners of your beard." Whoever is included in destroying is included in rounding. Women, since they are not included in destroying, are not included in rounding either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב הונא's reason: the פסוק links הקפה to השחתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts the two איסורים side by side, so they apply to the same people. Women have no beards and are not included in השחתה, so they are not included in הקפה either. That is why חובה could shave the boys. A grown man is bound by both, so he is liable even when the head he rounds belongs to a קטן.

keyTerms.meaning: destroying (shaving off) the corners of the beard

phrases.english: Rav Huna holds:
"You shall not round the corners of your head
and you shall not destroy the corners of your beard."
Whoever is included in the prohibition of destroying
is included in rounding,
and these women,
since they are not included in destroying,
they are not included in rounding either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First half of the answer to step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא ties הקפה to השחתה. Women, who are excluded from השחתה, are excluded from הקפה. A man is bound even when the head he rounds belongs to a קטן.

steps.title: רב אדא: the one who rounds is tied to the one who is rounded
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא learns that the one who shaves and the one being shaved are compared. Since a קטן is not punishable, the person who shaves him is not either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה holds: Both the one who rounds and the one who is rounded are included in the meaning. The one who rounds is compared to the one who is rounded: wherever the one rounded is liable, the one who rounds is also liable. This minor, since he himself is not subject to punishment, the one who rounds him is also not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב אדא's reason: the person shaving is liable only if the person being shaved is also liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא reads the plural פסוק as covering both people involved and compares them. A קטן is not punishable, so nobody who shaves him is punishable. In his view, any adult, man or woman, may shave a child, which is why he rejected רב הונא's ruling in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: the one whose head is rounded

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: הקפה follows השחתה, so women are exempt but a man shaving a קטן is liable. רב אדא: the one who shaves follows the one being shaved, so shaving a קטן is not punishable for anyone.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two comparisons. רב הונא compares two איסורים (head and beard). רב אדא compares two people (the one shaving and the one being shaved).

phrases.english: And Rav Adda bar Ahava holds:
Both the one who rounds and the one who is rounded are included in the meaning.
And the one who rounds is compared to the one who is rounded:
wherever the one who is rounded is liable,
the one who rounds is also liable.
And this minor,
since he himself
is not subject to punishment, so that he would be liable,
the one who rounds him is also not liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה סָבַר: אֶחָד הַמַּקִּיף וְאֶחָד הַנִּיקָּף בַּמַּשְׁמָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the answer to step 13, giving the opposing reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב אדא compares the one shaving to the one being shaved. Since a קטן is not punishable, anyone who shaves him is exempt.

steps.title: Is shaving the whole head an argument among תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that whether shaving the whole head counts as הקפה may be an argument among תנאים, and begins quoting a ברייתא about a מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that rounding the entire head is a dispute of תנאים? As the רבנן taught: "His head" — why does the verse need to say it? Because it says "You shall not round the corners of your head"...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question and starts quoting a ברייתא. This step is a setup, and the ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא asks why the פסוק about a מצורע's shaving mentions "his head" separately. Its answer starts by quoting the איסור of הקפה. The ברייתא's explanation, which continues after this point, will show whether shaving the whole head is treated as הקפה.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say (a suggestion the גמרא may later reject)
it is an argument among תנאים
why does the פסוק need to say it?

phrases.english: Shall we say that rounding the entire head
is a dispute of tanna'im?
As the Rabbis taught:
"His head" — why does the verse need to say it?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:9, the פסוק about a מצורע shaving all his hair.

phrases.english: Because it is stated:
